scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The same object looks different
scenes.caption: Kabir compares prepared images of a notebook and a cardboard box under bright light, dim light and a tight crop. The images and predictions are illustrative examples. No live vision model is running in this lesson.
scenes.dialogue: Does a familiar object guarantee a stable prediction?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A changed input
scenes.caption: The bright examples receive the intended labels. Under dim light or cropping, some prepared outputs change or request review. A single successful image does not establish robustness across conditions.
scenes.dialogue: Keep wrong labels separate from abstentions.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Features, layers and use
scenes.caption: Features describe patterns in the input. Layers transform representations. Training adjusts parameters using examples; inference uses the learned parameters on a new input. A confidence score is not a guarantee, and this activity does not reveal the internal workings of a real network.
scenes.dialogue: Concepts help explain the test, not prove a result.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the claim
scenes.caption: Can Kabir declare that all dim images fail, that the model is robust everywhere, or only that these supplied examples show changed outputs and need a bounded follow-up test?
scenes.dialogue: Let the sample limit the claim.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A bounded shift record
scenes.caption: Kabir records two correct bright outputs, one correct dim output and changed or review outcomes in the other conditions. The tiny prepared pack supports a classroom observation only. Unfamiliar conditions keep a human-review route.
scenes.dialogue: Do not generalise from six illustrative inputs.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the vision lab
scenes.caption: Match the network concepts, inspect each prepared image condition and classify its output as correct, wrong or review. State the limit and propose separate relevant evaluation before broader use.
scenes.dialogue: Changing the input can change the evidence.
